sections.h2: What kind of place is Oswego County, New York?
sections.html:
Oswego County fills a stretch of the eastern shore of Lake Ontario, north of Syracuse and northwest of Utica. It was formed in 1816 from parts of Oneida and Onondaga Counties, and its name comes from a Mohawk word for the point where the Oswego River pours into the lake. The city of Oswego is both the county seat and its largest city.

The county covers 1,312 square miles, and 360 of those, about 27 percent, are water. The Tug Hill Plateau reaches into the east end and gives the county its high point at 1,550 feet, while the 110 foot Salmon River Falls draws sightseers in the northeast. Oswego Harbor and Port Ontario are the two harbors.

Two cities, Oswego and Fulton, sit among 22 towns. Villages such as Phoenix, Pulaski, Central Square, Mexico and Sandy Creek are spread around Oneida Lake and the lake shore. SUNY Oswego and a Fulton branch campus of Cayuga County Community College, so two colleges are inside the county.

sections.h2: Does lake effect snow matter when selling an Oswego County house?
sections.html:
It can. In February 2007, a lake effect storm dropped more than 10 feet of snow on parts of the county, caused several roof collapses and led to a state of emergency. Roof condition is therefore worth documenting before you list or accept an offer.

If your roof has had repairs, keep the paperwork. If it has not been checked in years, a buyer paying cash and taking the house as-is will not ask you to make repairs first, and you can compare that against what a financed sale would require of you.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Oswego County?
sections.html:
The county does not run a single bill. Oswego County describes four separate bills: county and town, city, village and school. The county and town bill is issued January 1, the City of Oswego bill April 1, a Phoenix village bill March 1, other village bills June 1, and school bills in September or, in the Oswego City School District, October.

Local tax collectors take the first payments. Afterward, the County Treasurer is the enforcing officer for unpaid taxes everywhere except the City of Fulton, where the Fulton City Chamberlain enforces city, county and school tax. The county's Real Property Tax Services department, at 46 E. Bridge Street in Oswego, keeps tax maps and the assessment software. It states that it does not set assessments, collect taxes or keep payment receipts. The county's general line is 800-596-3200.

  • Assessments and exemption approvals: your town or city assessor.
  • Payments during the first collection window: the local tax collector named on your bill.
  • Delinquent taxes: the County Treasurer, or the Fulton Chamberlain for Fulton.
  • Deeds and surveys: the County Clerk.

sections.h2: What are the Oswego County tax dates and interest charges?
sections.html:
A county and town bill is due by January 31 without interest, with local collection running to March 31, and unpaid balances are returned to the county in mid-April. Interest is simple during local collection. Under the county's table, a county or town bill adds 1 percent after 30 days and 1 percent for each further month, a village bill adds 5 percent after 30 days, and a school bill adds 2 percent.

County and town bills may be paid in two equal installments unless an escrow account pays them. The first goes to the local collector by March 31, and the second goes to the County Treasurer by June 30 with interest on the remaining balance.

The county also warns that a tax bill that never arrives does not cancel the tax. Property taxes are levied against the land and buildings, so a sale transfers the problem to the buyer unless the balance is paid at closing.

sections.h2: How does an Oswego County tax foreclosure work?
sections.html:
Every property tax becomes a lien on the property and stays one until paid. The county starts Article 11 foreclosure on taxes that remain unpaid two years after they were issued, or four years for agricultural land. It holds two foreclosures each year in that way, and everything it forecloses on is sold together at one auction.

State law lets an owner redeem a delinquent lien by paying the enforcing officer before the redemption period ends, which is two years after the lien date unless the tax district sets another period (section 1110). Ask the Treasurer which date applies to your parcel.

The auction rules are strict. Buyers must have photo identification and a Social Security number, must not owe delinquent Oswego County tax, and must pay a buyer's premium and administrative fee, with any bid under $1,000 paid in full that day. The county sells tax-foreclosed houses as-is, does not warrant title, and gives the winner a tax deed. A former owner who is still behind has far more choices before the auction than on the day of it.

sections.h2: How do I sell an Oswego County house with taxes behind?
sections.html:
First find out who holds each balance. The Real Property Database shows original billed amounts, copies of county tax bills and delinquent payment status under the Tax Info link after you search for the parcel. The Treasurer can also set up a payment plan on unpaid taxes.

  1. Get a payoff in writing from the Treasurer, or from the Fulton Chamberlain for a Fulton house.
  2. Ask whether village or school balances have been re-levied onto the January county bill.
  3. Ask the date a foreclosure petition would be filed for your parcel.
  4. If you sell only part of a parcel, remember that a deed filed after March 1 leaves the old parcel on the bill.

A deed must be filed to move title in New York, and the county advises speaking to a lawyer about the type of deed. A buyer who closes quickly can pay the tax off from the sale, which ends the lien on your name before the foreclosure date.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent property tax in Oswego County?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer collects unpaid tax for every property except those in the City of Fulton, where the Fulton City Chamberlain does. Oswego city taxes go to the county one year after the city issues them. The county's general number is 800-596-3200.

faqs.q: How much interest does Oswego County add to a late bill?
faqs.a: During local collection, a county or town bill adds 1 percent after 30 days and 1 percent per further month. A village bill adds 5 percent after 30 days and a school bill adds 2 percent, each followed by 1 percent monthly. After the bill is returned to the county, interest compounds, so ask the Treasurer for the current payoff.

faqs.q: How long before Oswego County forecloses on unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: The county forecloses on taxes unpaid two years after they were issued, and four years for agricultural properties. Foreclosed parcels are sold together at one auction. The redemption period under state law is two years from the lien date unless the tax district sets another.

faqs.q: Can I split my Oswego County tax payment?
faqs.a: Yes for county and town bills, unless an escrow account pays them. Pay the first half to the local collector by March 31 and the second to the County Treasurer by June 30, with interest on the second half. City and school bills have their own split rules.

faqs.q: Does the county set my assessment in Oswego County?
faqs.a: No. Your town or city assessor sets the assessment and approves exemptions. The county Real Property Tax Services office keeps tax maps and the assessment software but states that it does not set assessments or collect taxes.
